previous_description: A data lifecycle management policy that governs how long data is retained and what action is taken when the retention period expires. Applicable across paradigms: time-series downsampling, key-value TTL, search index lifecycle, relational partition pruning, and archival strategies.
definition: A data lifecycle rule, declared in or enforced by the data store, that sets a maximum age for records in a collection or namespace and names the single action (delete, archive, downsample, move tier or compress) applied to records older than that age.

distinguish_from.when: the rule constrains or rejects writes, such as a TTL_CONSTRAINT requiring every key to carry an expiry, rather than removing or transforming data that has aged out
the symbol is the executable job, function or continuous query that performs the purge or rollup; the policy only declares age and action and triggers that logic
the downsampled result is a queryable derived collection such as a TimescaleDB continuous aggregate; the retention policy governs only when the source data expires
the code reacts to expiry or deletion events, such as a Redis keyspace EXPIRE notification listener, instead of defining when data expires

code_evidence: A migration or setup script containing InfluxDB `CREATE RETENTION POLICY ... DURATION 30d`, TimescaleDB `add_retention_policy('metrics', INTERVAL '90 days')`, or pg_partman `retention` settings on a partitioned table
An Elasticsearch ILM or OpenSearch ISM policy document with phases such as `delete.min_age`, or IaC declaring DynamoDB `TimeToLiveSpecification` or S3 lifecycle rules for a storage bucket
A MongoDB index created with `expireAfterSeconds`, or a scheduled purge job (cron or worker) issuing `DELETE ... WHERE created_at < now() - interval` or dropping old partitions

attribute_descriptions.name: enabled
attribute_descriptions.description: Whether the policy is currently active and enforced by the engine; set to false when the policy is defined but suspended (e.g., a disabled TimescaleDB job or paused ILM policy), otherwise true or omitted.

notes: A single duration and action cannot express multi-phase lifecycles such as ILM hot/warm/cold/delete; consider a phases array. Overlaps with collection.ttlDefault and MongoDB TTL indexes, so the boundary needs a rule. Format mismatch: retentionDuration uses ISO 8601 but downsampleInterval uses '1h'. The 'aggregates' edges duplicate 'governs'. An age-basis field (insert time or timestamp field) is missing.
